title: An Open Letter to Parents, Regarding Childhood Vacations
subtitle: I can't believe you put up with this
text:
I had no idea. I don't know how I could've had had an idea, but, heavens! The thought that a family vacation is somehow relaxing for families with young children? This is a vast conspiracy. Children, myself included, were a huge pain in the ass to travel with. My children are relatively well-behaved. I am blessed, when it comes to the attitudes and behaviors of my children.

Subscribe now

But …what a nightmare. It's hot. Or, it's too cold. But it's definitely also too hot. And now we have a sunburn. Let's go somewhere freezing. Why are we going somewhere hot? What are we gonna have dinner? Why isn't it the other thing? Can we go home now? This is the worst. I stepped on a rock. It hurts. One might be tempted to act:

I signed you up for kids club.

“Nooooooooooo.”

OK, you don't have to go to kids club. Why does any parent do this? What mass delusion led us to believe that taking vacations with our monstrous, or even extremely pleasant, children was an activity that would help us recharge?

It's like running a gauntlet. An awful, adorable, frustrating gauntlet with low frustration tolerance. I imagine it's like going on a work retreat if you happen to work at a tech bro led company, in the c- suite, but with less drugs and more sunburn-complications?

Academic literature exists on this topic!

The notion that leisure activities such as taking a vacation may act as a means of coping with stress, is a common belief. However, research framed under transactional theory suggests that taking a vacation trip may actually cause stress.1

This is not just my musing. I probably should've done a lit review before we booked the trip?

The good moments are perceived to be moments where all family members are content and happy, with no nagging or sulking, and in situations where the children are absorbed by activities, not necessarily with their parents.2

Mom, and the memory of my father, I owe you an apology. You schlepped my sister and I around the South of France in the boiling hot summer before cell phones and iPads were a thing. We had to be mollified with books…and the radio!

I can't even imagine.

I take back everything bad I ever said, and salute your parenting. To all parents who are about to vacation, I hope you get a vacation afterwards. You're gonna need it.

Unless you're at German-speaking middle manager sent to a hotel for four days— I presume not with their children— in which case? There are benefits in a randomized controlled trial. I'm not kidding.3

Share The Frontier Psychiatrists

1Zehrer, A., & Crotts, J. C. (2012). Vacation stress: The development of a vacation stress model among US vacation travelers. Tourism Review, 67(3), 41-55.

2Gram, M. (2005). Family holidays. A qualitative analysis of family holiday experiences. Scandinavian Journal of Hospitality and Tourism, 5(1), 2-22.

3Blank, C., Gatterer, K., Leichtfried, V., Pollhammer, D., Mair-Raggautz, M., Duschek, S., ... & Schobersberger, W. (2018). Short vacation improves stress-level and well-being in German-speaking middle-managers—A randomized controlled trial. International journal of environmental research and public health, 15(1), 130.
